title: Chicken Tagine with Apricots and Honey
subtitle: Moroccan chicken braise with dried fruit and warm spices
excerpt: This chicken tagine combines the savoury and sweet in the classic Moroccan style. Dried apricots soften into the sauce during the braise, adding sweetness and body. Honey and cinnamon round everything out. It is simpler than a lamb tagine and faster to cook.
sourceNotes: Sweet-savoury dishes with dried fruit, honey, and warm spices are a defining characteristic of Moroccan and broader North African cooking. The tradition traces to medieval Arab cookery and the influence of Persian and Andalusian cuisines that came with trade.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 2 months. Cool fully before freezing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made 1 day ahead. The flavours improve overnight.

content.text: Dried apricots are used here in place of fresh. They soften and dissolve slightly into the sauce, which thickens it naturally. Use unsulfured apricots if you can find them -- they have a deeper, more complex flavour.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pan. Brown the chicken thighs on both sides over high heat for 4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pan for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cinnamon and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute. Add 100g of dried apricots (roughly chopped), the honey, and the lemon juice.
Pour in the stock. Add the carrot pieces. Season with salt.
Return the chicken to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Taste the sauce. Add a squeeze more lemon if it needs balance. Serve with couscous or flatbread.

items.cause: Apricots and honey together are very sweet without enough acid
items.fix: Add more lemon juice -- start with half a lemon and taste as you go

items.cause: Not browned hard enough at the start
items.fix: Brown over the highest heat; the skin should be golden before the liquid is added

items.cause: Cut too small or cooked too long
items.fix: Cut carrots into chunky 3cm pieces; they should hold their shape in the finished dish

content.text: Sweet and savoury combinations are central to Moroccan cooking. Dried fruit, honey, and warm spices appear in dishes across the country, from the Atlas Mountains to the medinas of Fez and Marrakech. This tagine style is also common in Algeria and Tunisia, each with small regional variations in the spice balance.
